pamphlet_excerpts: Thedivide Rich Poor: Thedivide between rich and poor was widening, and most familieswere poor or close to it.
People Migrated Dirty: As people migrated to dirty, overcrowdedcities, they were more likely to become sick and less likely to beable to enjoy nature or get physical exercise.
Fact Britain Went: In fact, when Britain went to war in 1899, more than half the men whovolunteered for the army weren’t fit enough to fight.
Children Sides Atlantic: Children on both sides of the Atlantic Ocean suffered right alongwith their parents.
step_by_step_procedure: Beyond YMCAand Church-based: Beyond the YMCAand some church-based programs, few organized activities or sportsleagues were available for them toenjoy.
Worse Least Million: Even worse, at least 1.7 million American children under the age of 16 worked full time, sometimes workingas many as 12 hours a day in factoriesand.
Adults Grew Deeply: Many adults grew deeply concernedabout the problems of English and Child laborer, circa early 20th century American children.
Among Them Robert: Among them were Robert Baden-Powell, Ernest Thompson Seton, and Daniel Carter Beard.

pamphlet_excerpts: Born Denmark His: Born in Denmark in 1900, at 10 his brother gave him a copy of the Danish translation of Scouting for Boys.
Heearned Equivalent Eagle: Heearned the equivalent of Eagle Scout and became a Scoutmaster in Copenhagen.
Hillcourt Attended World: Hillcourt attended the first World Jamboree in London in 1920.
Went New York: In 1925, he went to New York, where he connected with Scouting friendsand soon earned a job with the BSA Supply Service.
step_by_step_procedure: West Hired Hillcourt: West hired Hillcourt towrite the first of many influential publications, the Handbook for Patrol Leaders.
Toadd Little Mystery: Toadd a little mystery, he adopted the nickname “Green Bar Bill” inreference to the two green bars on a patrol leader’s badge.
Test Ideas His: In 1935, to test ideas for his Scouting writing, he founded Troop 1 in Mendham, New Jersey.
Part Wood Courses: In 1936 he was part of the first Wood Badge courses in the United States, and in 1948 was Scoutmaster for the first two standard American courses.

pamphlet_excerpts: BSA Created Program: In 1935, the BSA created a program called Explorer Scouts asone option in Senior Scouting.
Offered Older Boy: It offered to older Boy Scouts a land-based alternative to Sea Scouting.
Explorer Initially Wore: Explorer Scouts initially wore the same uniform as Boy Scouts, although it featured an “Explorer Scout, BSA” stripover the right pocket.
Forest-green Uniform: In the 1940s, a forest-green uniform wasintroduced, and Explorer Scout units began to be called postsinstead of troops.
step_by_step_procedure: Explorer Got Theirown: Explorer Scouts got theirown advancement programin 1944.
Ranks Apprentice Woodsman: The four ranks, Apprentice, Woodsman, Frontiersman, and Ranger, corresponded to the four ranksin Sea Scouting.
Explorer Scoutsbecame Simply: In 1949, Explorer Scoutsbecame simply Explorers, and the program’s focus wasexpanded to include socialactivities, service opportunities.
Posts Beganto Specialize: More and more, posts beganto specialize in specific careersor hobbies.

requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Attend either a Scouting America National Jamboree, OR World Scout Jamboree, OR a national Scouting America high-adventure base. While there, keep a journal documenting your day-to-day experiences. Upon your return, report to your counselor what you did, saw, and learned. You may include photos, brochures, and other documents in your report. (b) Write or visit the National Scouting Museum. Obtain information about this facility. Give a short report on what you think the role of this museum is in the Scouting program. (c) Visit an exhibit of Scouting memorabilia or a local museum with a Scouting history gallery, or (with your parent or guardian's permission and counselor's approval) visit with someone in your council who is recognized as a dedicated Scouting historian or memorabilia collector. Learn what you can about the history of Scouting America. Give a short report to your counselor on what you saw and learned.

pamphlet_excerpts: Baden-Powell Seton Beard: Baden-Powell, Seton, Beard, and the Birth of Scouting ing concepts from The Birch Bark Roll of the Woodcraft Indians (1906) by Ernest Thompson Seton.
Aids Focused: Aids to Scouting focused on militaryscouting and self-reliance skillslearned from Frederick Russell Burnham, the British Army Chief of Scouts.
Baden-Powell Recruited: Baden-Powell recruited andtrained boys as cadets during the siege, leading to Aids to Scouting’s use in British schools for teaching observation.
Book Publication Sparked: The book’s publication sparked widespreadinterest, leading to the formation of Scout patrolsworldwide.
step_by_step_procedure: End Century Nearly: By the end of the 20th century, nearly 150 million copies of Scouting for Boys had beenpublished, making it one of the best-selling books ofall time.
Thanks Boys Quicklyspread: Thanks to Scouting for Boys, Scouting quicklyspread through England, the British colonies, andbeyond.
Early People America: As early as 1908, people in America werebuying copies of the book and starting their owntroops.
Woman Burnside Kentucky: A woman in Burnside, Kentucky, started agroup she called the “Eagle Troop” that year.

Newspaper Reporters Learn: Newspaper reporters learn to ask questions insix categories, who, what, when, where, why, and how, andit’s a good idea to cover all of those areas.
Start List Basic: Start your list with basic factual questions: What troop wereyou in?.
step_by_step_procedure: Then Move Questions: Then, move on to questions like these: • Why did you join Scouting?
Worst Did Ever: Your worst? • Did you ever go to a jamboree or on a high-adventure trip?.
Based Knowledge History: Based on your knowledge of Scouting history, you willbe able to come up with more specific questions.
Write Questions Open-ended: Be sure to write questions that are open-ended and thatwill encourage your subject to tell stories.

requirements.lead_text: Careers. Do ONE of the following:
requirements.req_text: Careers. Do ONE of the following: (a) Explore careers related to Scouting. Research one career to learn about the training and education needed, costs, job prospects, salary, job duties, and career advancement. With permission of your parent or guardian, your research methods may include an internet or library search, an interview with a professional in the field, or a visit to a location where people in this career work. Discuss with your counselor both your findings and what about this profession might make it an interesting career. (b) Explore how you could use knowledge and skills from this merit badge to serve as a Scouting volunteer. Research any training needed, expenses, and how you could serve as a unit, district, council, regional, or national volunteer. Discuss with your counselor what short-term and long-term goals you might have if you pursued this.

pamphlet_excerpts: BSA Introduced Varsity: In 1984, the BSA introduced Varsity Scouting, aimedat boys ages 14 but not yet 18 years old.
Varsity Sports Terminology: Varsity Scouting used sports terminology and offered highadventure activities geared for older Scouts.
Varsity Same Advancement: Varsity Scouts used the same advancement program as Boy Scouts, but they could also earn the Denali Award.

step_by_step_procedure: Carey Massachusetts Started: Carey of Massachusetts started a Sea Scout group using his schooner, the Pioneer.
Programlimped Along: The programlimped along until Commander Thomas J.
Keane Revamped Program: Keane revamped the program, introducing an advancementprogram that included four ranks: Apprentice, Ordinary, Able, and Quartermaster.
Sea Became Sea: Sea Scouting became known as Sea Exploring in 1949, but the program didn’t change much.
